_README: Supplies the bits Google Scholar can't expose. scripts/fetch_scholar.py scrapes Scholar, then merges this file on top, keyed by citation_id.
The curated 'publications' entries are authoritative for titles, authors, venues, years, statuses, and canonical links. Scholar refreshes citation counts without rewriting those fields.

Sync policy — first-author only in both sections. Published journal/conference → full-detail Publications cards. arXiv preprints + under-review → compact Preprints rows (title · venue · year, no authors/citations).
Use 'manual_publications' for accepted papers whose conference metadata has not reached Scholar yet; matching by title prevents a duplicate when Scholar catches up.
Preprints don't need overrides in most cases; per-paper 'venue_short' and 'links' still work if you want to customize a row.
Corresponding authors are per-paper only. If a paper's entry doesn't list 'corresponding', no author is marked (no global default anymore).
By design we don't carry impact factors, page numbers, or long conference titles — the Publications layout shows venue + year + citations, all auto-tracked from Scholar.

Per-paper display fields: 'venue_badge' (short tag above the title, e.g. "SC '26"), 'venue_full' (full venue name under the authors; the year is appended), 'image' (a teaser figure under assets/img/papers/). 'summary' is kept in the data but not shown.

manual_publications.venue_full: The International Conference for High Performance Computing, Networking, Storage, and Analysis (SC)
manual_publications.summary: QSAD recasts structure prediction for peptides in binding pockets as Hamiltonian sampling, replacing iterative optimization. Run entirely on IBM Heron R2 over 101 peptides, it was 27–71% more accurate than every AI and quantum baseline we tested and used 27× less quantum time than VQE.
manual_publications.title: Quantum Sampling Architecture for Protein Structure Reconstruction on Utility-Scale Hardware

Q7Ybs-gAAAAJ:LkGwnXOMwfcC.summary: We pose structure prediction for short, flexible binding-site fragments as a VQE ground-state problem on a tetrahedral lattice, and ran every experiment on the IBM quantum processor at Cleveland Clinic. On 30 fragments the predictions beat AlphaFold3 and classical baselines in both RMSD and docking.
Q7Ybs-gAAAAJ:LkGwnXOMwfcC.title: A Quantum Framework for Protein Binding-Site Structure Prediction on Utility-Level Quantum Processors

Q7Ybs-gAAAAJ:Tyk-4Ss8FVUC.venue_full: The International Conference for High Performance Computing, Networking, Storage, and Analysis (SC)
Q7Ybs-gAAAAJ:Tyk-4Ss8FVUC.summary: A dataset of protein fragment structures predicted on utility-level quantum computers, built for ligand docking. Each fragment comes with its quantum run metadata (qubits, circuit depth, energies, runtime) and its docking and RMSD results.
Q7Ybs-gAAAAJ:Tyk-4Ss8FVUC.title: QDockBank: A Dataset for Ligand Docking on Protein Fragments Predicted on Utility-Level Quantum Computers

Q7Ybs-gAAAAJ:eQOLeE2rZwMC.summary: We fuse VQE energies from a 127-qubit IBM processor with secondary-structure and dihedral-angle statistics from the NSP3 network. The combined energy picks out native-like structures more reliably, reaching a mean RMSD of 4.9 Å on 75 protein fragments, ahead of AlphaFold3 and ColabFold.
Q7Ybs-gAAAAJ:eQOLeE2rZwMC.title: A Hybrid Quantum-AI Framework for Protein Structure Prediction on NISQ Devices

Q7Ybs-gAAAAJ:Se3iqnhoufwC.summary: Qronecker compresses quantum-chemistry qubit Hamiltonians with low-rank Kronecker decompositions computed directly in Pauli coefficient space, and returns a worst-case energy certificate for each choice of rank and cut. Evaluated on hundreds of molecules up to 30 qubits.
Q7Ybs-gAAAAJ:Se3iqnhoufwC.title: Qronecker: A Certifiable Kronecker Compression Primitive for Quantum-Chemistry Hamiltonians
